whatsIncluded.metaDescription: What every NomadTrip journey includes: yurt stays, meals, transport, local guides and host families, activities and support, and what is not included.
whatsIncluded.title: What's included
whatsIncluded.intro: Every NomadTrip journey is built around the same essentials: yurt stays, meals, local guides and transport in Kyrgyzstan. Here is what that means in practice.

accommodation.title: Accommodation
accommodation.body: Every night of every trip is spent in a yurt camp run by a local family.

points.1: A yurt has a wooden lattice frame, a felt cover and a shanyrak, the ring at the top of the roof that lets in light and, at night, sometimes the stars.
points.2: You sleep on tushuk mattresses, thick felt-and-wool mattresses laid on the floor, with blankets provided.
points.3: Many yurts have a small stove, which camps usually light at night when it gets cold.
points.4: Camps usually have shared toilets and, at some, simple shared showers. Facilities are basic and vary between camps.
points.5: Yurts are shared with other travelers by default. A private yurt for your group is available for a supplement when you book.

meals.title: Meals
meals.body: Meals are included on trip days and are cooked by your hosts at the camps.

points.1: Expect traditional, hearty food: bread, dairy, soups and stews, plenty of meat, fresh boorsok (fried dough) and tea.
points.2: Kymyz, fermented mare's milk, may be offered as a welcome. You are free to decline or take just a sip.
points.3: Vegetarian, vegan, halal, gluten-free and other needs can be noted when you book. Options in remote camps can be limited, so early notice helps.
points.4: Tea is served with meals, and your guide will tell you about drinking water at each camp.

transport.title: Transport
transport.body: Transport within Kyrgyzstan is included, between camps and to the places on your itinerary.

points.1: Road transfers use vehicles suited to the route. Some routes follow rough mountain roads.
points.2: Airport pickup from Bishkek (Manas, FRU) or Osh (OSS) is available at no extra charge. Choose it when you book.
points.3: On riding trips you cover part of the route on horseback.

guides.title: Guides and hosts
guides.body: Local guides and host families look after you from the first day to the last.

points.1: Every trip has a guide who knows the route, the weather and the people, and who helps with language and customs.
points.2: Camps are run by local herder families who cook, host and share their way of life with you.
points.3: If you would like a guide who speaks a particular language, tell us before you book and we will explain what is possible.

activities.title: Activities
activities.body: Riding, walking and cultural visits are part of each trip's itinerary.

points.1: Horse rides with local handlers. Horses on our trips are used to beginners, so tell us your experience level.
points.2: Hikes and walks from gentle to demanding. The difficulty level is listed on every trip.
points.3: Cultural visits and demonstrations, such as eagle hunting or felt-making, where they are part of the itinerary.
points.4: The day-by-day plan on each trip page shows exactly what is planned.

safety.title: Safety and support
safety.body: Your guide is with you throughout the trip, and a first-aid kit travels with the group.

points.1: Your guide knows the route and the weather and helps if plans need to change.
points.2: Coverage is often absent in high valleys and at remote camps, so expect to be offline for part of the trip.
points.3: Tell us about health conditions when you book. If you have heart, lung or other concerns, talk to your doctor before a high-altitude trip.

whatsIncluded.notIncludedIntro: These are not part of the trip price. Please arrange them yourself.

notIncluded.1: International flights to and from Kyrgyzstan
notIncluded.6: Personal expenses, such as souvenirs and extra snacks

experiences.metaDescription: Horse riding, eagle hunting, felt-making, nomad cooking, trekking, mountain lakes, stargazing and komuz music on NomadTrip journeys.
experiences.title: Experiences
experiences.intro: The moments you will remember from a yurt journey: on horseback, around the table and under the stars.
experiences.noTrips: Ask us if you would like to add this to your trip.

horseRiding.title: Horse riding
horseRiding.body: Ride along lake shores and over mountain passes with local herders and handlers. Horses on our trips are used to beginners, and a handler helps you along. Tell us your experience level when you book.

eagleHunting.title: Eagle hunting
eagleHunting.body: Meet a berkutchi, a traditional eagle hunter, and watch a demonstration with a golden eagle. It is a living tradition of Kyrgyz herders.

feltMaking.title: Felt-making
feltMaking.body: See how wool is laid out, wetted and rolled into felt, the material of yurt walls and floors. Felt is also made into the shyrdak and ala-kiyiz rugs you will see in every yurt.

nomadCooking.title: Nomad cooking and kymyz
nomadCooking.body: Share the table with your hosts: fresh boorsok, bread, tea and, if you like, a sip of kymyz, fermented mare's milk. Meals are traditional, hearty and cooked by the camp family.

trekking.title: Trekking and passes
trekking.body: Walk through spruce forest, river valleys and high passes. Walks range from gentle to demanding at altitude, so choose the difficulty that suits you.

mountainLakes.title: Mountain lakes
mountainLakes.body: Alpine lakes such as Song-Kul, Kel-Suu, Sary-Chelek and Tulpar-Kol are highlights of several routes. Expect water, pasture and peaks far from the road.

stargazing.title: Stargazing
stargazing.body: Far from city lights, nights at altitude are dark. On a clear night you can see the Milky Way from your yurt door.

komuz.title: Komuz music
komuz.body: The komuz is a three-stringed Kyrgyz lute that accompanies songs and epic tales. Evenings with your hosts can include music and storytelling.
